description: Uses normalized deep-level orderbook ratio (fraction of each side at levels 3-5 vs total) to detect MM positioning in narrow mid-price band (0.45-0.55) markets during UTC 0-6 hours. Signal = bid_deep_frac - ask_deep_frac, bounded [-1,1]. 2s aggregation window with median, threshold 0.25.
hypothesis: In the most uncertain markets (true coin-flip territory, mid_price 0.45-0.55), MM positioning at deeper orderbook levels carries maximum informational content since there is no strong prior to anchor prices. Lower threshold (0.25) compensates for reduced universe size. UTC 0-6 filter targets low-activity hours where MM signals are less noisy.
next_steps: The exact hypothesis (2s window, T=0.25, UTC 0-6, 0.45-0.55 band) produces 50.0% WR on 24 trades — no predictive power, PnL negative purely from fees. Grid search without the UTC filter found W=5000ms T=0.25 at 57.9% WR on 95 trades, but OOS split shows inconsistency (first half 53.3% WR vs second half 62.0% WR), suggesting overfitting. The UTC 0-6 filter reduces the universe to only 34 markets (24 resolved), too small for reliable inference. The deep_level_ratio signal is well-behaved after normalization but does not consistently predict direction in coin-flip markets. Consider: (1) wider mid-price band where a prior exists to lean on, (2) signal as feature in multi-factor model, (3) time-series dynamics (signal changes) rather than level.
